title: When an Algorithm Should Ask for Help
section: 讲话 / 报道 / 讲座
transcript:
We often judge an automatic system by the number of decisions it gets right. That measure overlooks an equally important ability: recognizing when a decision should be passed to a person. Consider a programme that sorts photographs of manufactured parts. It may perform well on familiar objects while confidently misclassifying a new component that was never included in its training.

In one classroom demonstration, an engineering lecturer gave students an image classifier trained to distinguish three kinds of metal fitting. The students first tested it using photographs taken under the same lighting as the training pictures. Its accuracy was impressive. They then introduced a fourth fitting, partly wrapped in protective paper. The programme still assigned each image to one of the original categories, often with a high confidence score.

The lecturer explained that confidence represented the programme's preference among the available answers. It did not prove that those answers included the correct one. To address this limitation, the class added a separate check that compared the new image with the range of images seen during training. Unusual images were sent to a human reviewer before classification.

The revised system made fewer unsupported decisions, but it also referred some perfectly ordinary parts for review when shadows changed their appearance. Tightening the threshold reduced those interruptions while allowing more unfamiliar objects through. There was no single threshold that eliminated both problems.

The exercise illustrates why human involvement should be designed into an automated process rather than added only after a failure. The appropriate balance depends on the consequences of an error and the cost of review. A factory inspecting inexpensive packaging may accept a different balance from one checking components used in aircraft.

questions.prompt: What ability does the lecturer say ordinary accuracy measures overlook?
options: Recognizing when human assistance is needed.
Processing images taken in bright light.
Learning the names of metal materials.
Sorting familiar objects into known categories.
questions.answer: Recognizing when human assistance is needed.
questions.explanation: 开头指出正确率忽略了系统能否识别应交给人工处理的情况。

questions.prompt: Why was a high confidence score potentially misleading?
options: It recorded the reviewer’s personal preference.
It was calculated before the photograph was taken.
It indicated a preference among answers that might all be wrong.
It was based only on the size of the image file.
questions.answer: It indicated a preference among answers that might all be wrong.
questions.explanation: 高置信度仅表示在既有类别中偏好某一项，不代表正确类别确实包含在其中。

questions.prompt: What drawback appeared after unusual images were referred to a reviewer?
options: The programme stopped recognizing all familiar fittings.
Ordinary parts sometimes required unnecessary human review.
The students could no longer change the threshold.
All unfamiliar objects were automatically rejected as defective.
questions.answer: Ordinary parts sometimes required unnecessary human review.
questions.explanation: 阴影改变外观后，一些普通零件也被当成异常图片转人工。

questions.prompt: What should influence the choice of a review threshold?
options: The number of students operating the programme.
The age of the factory building.
Whether all photographs use the same file name.
The consequences of mistakes and the expense of review.
questions.answer: The consequences of mistakes and the expense of review.
questions.explanation: 结尾说明阈值取决于错误后果及人工审核成本。
